newsitem.title: DENMARK: Clinton condemns N. Ireland violence.
newsitem.headline: Clinton condemns N. Ireland violence.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Saturday praised Northen Ireland's Protestant Orange Order for rerouting parades away from volatile areas and condemned as "inexcusable" attacks on security forces and two youths.

"I welcome the decision of the Orange Order and its local lodges to voluntarily call off and reroute the contentious parades scheduled for this weekend," Clinton said in a statement issued by the White House as he ended an eight-day trip to Europe.

"I hope that the people of both communities redouble their efforts to reach accommodation on other contentious parades in a spirit of goodwill and generosity and reject the inexcusable violence that we saw in Northern Ireland today," he said.

Suspected Irish Republican gunmen shot and wounded five security personnel and two Protestant teenagers as the Orange Order, founded by Protestants to celebrate their faith and loyalty to Britain, staged hundreds of small parades.

The Order scrapped marches planned through volatile areas in Belfast, Newry and Armagh and rerouted another parade in Londonderry in a landmark decision after decades of refusal to heed Catholics who saw such demonstrations as intimidation.

"The people of North Ireland have the United States' unwavering support to build on this moment of hope to seek a lasting settlement to the conflict that has divided them for far too long," Clinton said.
Clinton has paid particular interest in peace efforts for Northern Ireland, and in 1995 became the first U.S. president to visit the troubled province.
